newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Public Bank revises price of rights.
newsitem.headline: Public Bank revises price of rights.

text.p: Malaysia's Public Bank Bhd said on Thursday it was revising the price of a proposed rights issue for the foreign tranche of its stock.

Holders of the foreign stock will pay up to 3.30 ringgit per share in the rights issue, instead of a fixed price of 3.30 ringgit as previously announced, the company said in a statement issued by its merchant banker.
The price of the foreign-share rights will be determined at a later date based on a five day weighted average market price preceding the price-fixing date, said Public Bank.
The bank had proposed a one-for-five rights issue for both the local shares at 2.20 riniggit and at 3.30 ringgit per share for the foreign tranche.

Public Bank, Malaysia's fourth largest banking group, said the revision was made "after taking into consideration the current performance of the foreign shares on the KLSE (Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange)".

The foreign tranche of the bank's stock plunged on Wednesday and early on Thursday on market interpretations of a company circular that it was allowing foreign investors to buy the local tranche of the stock.
Public Bank foreign shares fell to a 12-month low of 3.78 ringgit on Thursday, before rebounding to close at 4.02, up 10 cents.
Public Bank local shares closed eight cents lower to 3.48, after surging on Wednesday and early Thursday.
The foreign tranche of the stock had traditionally traded at a premium to the local tranche as foreign investors were previously allowed only to buy the 'foreign' shares.
